Subject: HaloHealth discovery synthesis & architecture alignment

Thanks again for the time earlier today — concise recap below plus proposed next steps so we can validate architecture and SLOs before the technical deep-dive. Please reply with corrections.

Quick summary of pain and goals
- Pain: variance in inference latency causing poor UX for real-time triage; unpredictable token cost during peak batch processing; no current plan for model fallback when GPU capacity is constrained.
- Goal: sub-200ms p95 for single-request interactive flows, sustain ~12k concurrent qps-equivalent (batched) for nightly ingestion, and lower per-token cost by ~30% vs current hosted provider.

Key technical constraints you shared
- Model family: currently evaluating open LLMs (7B–13B) for clinical summarization; want option to move to quantized 8-bit variants.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in prompts, requires VPC + KMS; SOC 2 and audit logs are must-haves.
- KV cache: 90% of requests have conversational prefix reuse; expect to benefit from prefix/KV caching.

SLOs and suggested acceptance criteria (proposal)
- Interactive flows (single-shot summarization): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 200ms for <=1024 tokens response when served from warm KV cache.
- Bulk ingestion (batched scoring): aggregate throughput target 120k tokens/sec sustained for nightly windows with 2x burst capacity.
- Availability: 99.9% platform availability for production inference with regional fallback.

Preliminary topology options (tradeoffs)
- Private Dedicated (on VPC): best for PHI, simpler compliance; predictable latency but higher fixed cost.
- Hybrid: Dedicated for interactive tier + burst to hosted for non-PHI nightly batch; saves cost but adds routing complexity and controls for PHI data.

Requested artifacts from HaloHealth before deep-dive
1) 3 days of representative traffic (sampled requests + token distributions) — CSV or JSONL.
2) Typical prompt schemas and max response length requirements.
3) Any internal compliance checklist (SOC 2 control owners, KMS usage).

Attachments: shared a small sample mapping and a template we use for traffic samples (20280410-halohealth-mapping.csv, halohealth-sample-traffic.jsonl).

Next steps / proposed timeline
- HaloHealth provides requested samples by EOD Thu 4/13.
- We run a short profiling job on those samples and deliver a 1-page capacity & topology recommendation (by Mon 4/17).
- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive the week of 4/17 — Rishi to lead server/runtime discussion.

If that all looks good I’ll circulate a calendar invite with a proposed agenda.

Thanks,

Thanks Jasmine — useful write-up. A few clarifications from our side: we can provide the traffic sample as JSONL (anonymized) by Thursday. Some clarifications below — copying our eng alias for visibility.

On Apr 10, 2028, at 3:20 PM, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Key technical constraints you shared
> - Model family: currently evaluating open LLMs (7B–13B) for clinical summarization; want option to move to quantized 8-bit variants.

Two clarifications:
- Model: our evaluation is focused on a tuned 13B that currently runs at ~220ms median on our existing provider for a 512-token output. We want to understand whether moving to a quantized 8-bit variant on Redwood will reduce cost enough without regressing accuracy.
- PHI: we cannot send raw PHI outside the VPC. We’ll sanitize and provide masked samples, but the architecture needs to assume PHI-local processing.

Questions for the deep-dive:
1) Can Redwood demonstrate p95 numbers for a quantized 13B on NVidia A10 / G5 instances for 512-token responses?
2) What controls exist to ensure routing never leaves the VPC for PHI-tagged requests?

We’re also interested in a hybrid approach if it means we can keep interactive flows in VPC and push non-PHI bulk to a hosted pool.

—Miguel

Adding technical notes ahead of the deep-dive — high level answers and what we’ll validate when we profile your samples.

1) Quantized 13B p95 on common configs
- On A10 (fp16 kernel) we typically see p50 ~80–120ms and p95 ~200–350ms for 512-token responses depending on batching and KV warm hit-rate.
- On G5 (Ampere) with optimized kernels and int8 quantization path we can hit p95 closer to 160–220ms for similar response lengths, but accuracy depends on the quantization recipe and any fine-tuning.

2) PHI routing and VPC controls
- Private deployment option: control plane runs in Redwood but inference plane can be placed inside your VPC (no egress for request payloads).
- KMS/HSM integration for key management and in-flight encryption for cache objects.
- We’ll include proof points (audit log sample) in the profiling deliverable.

3) Throughput and batching considerations
- For nightly batch scoring we recommend a dedicated GPU pool with autoscaling and a separate queue for non-PHI requests to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- We’ll benchmark sample traffic to produce an expected tokens/sec vs cost curve and a recommended batching window.

Action items (Rishi)
- Run initial profiling on the provided JSONL samples and return a short report with: latency distribution (p50/p95), suggested batch/window sizing, KV hit assumptions, and an estimated cost per 1M tokens on both dedicated and hosted variants. (ETA: Mon 4/17)
- Provide a short appendix showing quantization tradeoffs for the candidate 13B model (accuracy vs memory).

I’ll build a benchmark matrix for the deep-dive.

—Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
